source_lines.34: In binary64 RNE take A=((1,1),(0,2^-27)). Its determinant 2^-27 is nonzero. The exact Gram matrix is A^T A=((1,1),(1,1+2^-54)). The spacing above 1 is 2^-52, so the midpoint is 1+2^-53; 1+2^-54 lies strictly below it and rounds to 1. Thus the formed Gram matrix has equal rows and is singular. Reduced QR works directly on A and avoids forming this rounded Gram matrix; the computed stability statement remains conditional on its own hypotheses.

The relative data change is 2^-40 while the relative solution change is 1. Thus backward stability does not imply small forward error for an ill-conditioned design.
